claim: Dialyzed conditioned media from wild-type HAP1 cells supported wild-type cell growth, increasing growth by 50% compared to non-dialyzed media.
source: Wild-type cells similarly responded to dialyzed media from both genotypes, increasing growth by 50% as compared to non-dialyzed media (Figure 1A compare columns 1, 3 and 2, 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A, which presents cell number determinations using Alamar blue assay.

claim: Dialyzed conditioned media from SLC25A1Δ cells fed onto wild-type cells doubled their number.
source: SLC25A1Δ cells fed with wild-type dialyzed conditioned media doubled in number (Figure 1A, compare columns 5 and 7)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A comparing cell numbers under different media conditions.

claim: Dialyzed conditioned media from SLC25A1Δ cells did not support SLC25A1Δ cell growth as well as media from wild-type cells.
source: dialyzed conditioned media from SLC25A1Δ cells fed onto themselves did not support their growth as compared to media from wild-type cells (Figure 1A compare columns 7–8 and 6–8).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A comparing growth of SLC25A1Δ cells in different conditioned media.

claim: 668 proteins significantly changed their expression in SLC25A1Δ cells compared to 110 proteins in SLC25A4Δ cells.
source: 668 proteins significantly changed their expression in SLC25A1Δ cells compared to 110 proteins in SLC25A4Δ cells (log2 fold of change of 0.5 and p<0.05, Figure 1B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by TMT proteomic data shown in volcano plots in Figure 1B and C.

claim: The SLC25A1Δ transcriptome was represented by 2433 transcripts whose expression was changed, a fourfold difference compared to the 560 transcripts found in SLC25A4Δ cells.
source: the SLC25A1Δ transcriptome was represented by 2433 transcripts whose expression was changed in SLC25A1-null cells, a fourfold difference compared to the 560 transcripts found in SLC25A4Δ cells (log2 fold of change of 1 and p<0.001, Figure 1F and G).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNAseq data shown in volcano plots in Figure 1F and G.

claim: Only 84 proteins and 385 mRNAs were shared by both SLC25A1Δ and SLC25A4Δ genotypes.
source: Despite the abundance of altered gene products in these SLC25A1Δ and SLC25A4Δ datasets, there was limited overlap in proteomes and transcriptomes, with only 84 proteins and 385 mRNAs shared by both genotypes (Figure 1J).
evidence: The claim is supported by Venn diagram analysis shown in Figure 1J comparing proteome and transcriptome hits.

claim: 27 proteins and transcripts were similarly modified in both SLC25A1Δ and SLC25A4Δ datasets.
source: the congruency of the shared proteomes and transcriptomes reached only 0.9% of all the gene products whose expression was modified. This represents 27 proteins and transcripts similarly modified in SLC25A1Δ and SLC25A4Δ datasets (Figure 1J).
evidence: The claim is supported by Venn diagram analysis shown in Figure 1J.

claim: APOE was one of five factors annotated to the secreted human proteome that were common hits in SLC25A1Δ and SLC25A4Δ datasets.
source: Of these 27 common hits, one was annotated to mitochondria, FASTKD2, and five were annotated to the secreted human proteome, including soluble proteins such as apolipoprotein E (APOE) and cytokine receptor-like factor 1 (CRLF1; Elson et al., 1998; Wernette-Hammond et al., 1989; Figure 1J).
evidence: The claim is supported by annotation analysis of common hits shown in Figure 1J and cited references.

claim: APOE protein and transcript were among the most upregulated factors in both SLC25A1Δ and SLC25A4Δ cells.
source: APOE protein and transcript were among the most upregulated factors in both SLC25A1Δ and SLC25A4Δ cells (Figure 1B–C and F–G).
evidence: The claim is supported by proteomic and transcriptomic data shown in Figure 1B-C and F-G.

claim: Close to 10% of all the SLC25A1Δ and SLC25A4Δ proteome hits were proteins annotated to mitochondria.
source: Close to 10% of all the SLC25A1Δ and SLC25A4Δ proteome hits were proteins annotated to mitochondria, with a discrete overlap of 10 mitochondrial proteins between these two mutant genotypes
evidence: The claim is supported by annotation analysis of proteome hits with Mitocarta 3.0.

claim: 10 mitochondrial proteins overlapped between SLC25A1Δ and SLC25A4Δ genotypes, mostly downregulated constituents of complex III of the electron transport chain.
source: with a discrete overlap of 10 mitochondrial proteins between these two mutant genotypes, mostly downregulated constituents of complex III of the electron transport chain (Figure 1K, UQCRB11, UQCRB, UQCRC2, and UQCRQ)
evidence: The claim is supported by Venn diagram and protein identification shown in Figure 1K.

claim: COX7A2L, a factor required for the assembly of respiratory supercomplexes, was among the 10 overlapping mitochondrial proteins in SLC25A1Δ and SLC25A4Δ cells.
source: as well as a factor required for the assembly of respiratory supercomplexes, COX7A2L (Figure 1K; Lobo-Jarne et al., 2018).
evidence: The claim is supported by protein identification in Figure 1K and cited reference about COX7A2L function.

claim: The enrichment of secreted proteome annotated proteins was modest yet significant in SLC25A1Δ and SLC25A4Δ cells.
source: The enrichment of secreted proteome annotated proteins was modest yet significant in SLC25A1Δ and SLC25A4Δ cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by enrichment analysis of secretome-annotated proteins.

claim: The degree of enrichment in components of the secretome was comparable to the enrichment of Mitocarta 3.0 annotated proteins in both SLC25A1Δ and SLC25A4Δ mitochondrial mutants.
source: this degree of enrichment in components of the secretome was comparable to the enrichment of Mitocarta 3.0 annotated proteins in both mitochondrial mutants (Figure 1L, M and N).
evidence: The claim is supported by enrichment analysis shown in Figure 1L, M and N.

claim: Mutations affecting two inner mitochondrial membrane transporters, SLC25A1 and SLC25A4, similarly affect the secreted and mitochondrial proteomes.
source: These results show that mutations affecting two inner mitochondrial membrane transporters, SLC25A1 and SLC25A4, similarly affect the secreted and mitochondrial proteomes.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the enrichment analysis and comparison of secretome and mitochondrial proteome changes.

claim: The most prominent ontology annotated to up-regulated SLC25A1Δ proteome and transcriptome hits was steroid biosynthesis.
source: the most prominent ontology annotated to up-regulated SLC25A1Δ proteome and transcriptome hits was steroid biosynthesis (KEGG:00100, Bonferroni corrected P=3.6E-8 and 1.9E-8 for the transcriptome and proteome, respectively; Figure 1O–P).
evidence: The claim is supported by gene ontology analysis shown in Figure 1O-P with statistical significance values.

claim: The expression of genes annotated to sterol biosynthesis ontologies was not modified in SLC25A4Δ mutants.
source: However, the expression of genes annotated to sterol biosynthesis ontologies was not modified in SLC25A4Δ mutants, even though the proteome and transcriptome of SLC25A4Δ cells showed increased expression of APOE, a cholesterol transport lipoprotein.
evidence: The claim is supported by gene ontology analysis comparing SLC25A1Δ and SLC25A4Δ mutants.

claim: Expression of APOE and other hits common between SLC25A1Δ and SLC25A4Δ mutant genotypes occurs independently from modifications in cholesterol synthesis pathways.
source: These findings suggest that expression of APOE and other hits common between these two mutant genotypes occurs independently from modifications in cholesterol synthesis pathways.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that APOE is upregulated in both mutants but sterol biosynthesis genes are only upregulated in SLC25A1Δ.

claim: APOE protein expression and secretion were increased approximately 5-20 times in two CRISPR SLC25A1Δ clones and SLC25A4Δ cells.
source: APOE protein expression and secretion into media were increased ~5–20 times in two CRISPR SLC25A1Δ clones and SLC25A4Δ cells (Figure 2A compare column 1 with 2–4 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1 compare columns 1, 3, and 5 with 7, 9, and 11).
evidence: The claim is supported by MesoScale ELISA data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: APOE signal in complete media unexposed to cells was undetectable.
source: APOE signal in complete media unexposed to cells was undetectable (Figure 2A compare media columns 1 with 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by MesoScale ELISA data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: APOE present in media and cells was sensitive to protein synthesis inhibition with cycloheximide.
source: APOE present in media and cells was sensitive to protein synthesis inhibition with cycloheximide (Figure 2—figure supplement 1 compare columns 1–2 and 7–8)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data with cycloheximide treatment shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: APOE present in media and cells was sensitive to disruption of the secretory pathway with brefeldin A.
source: and to disruption of the secretory pathway with brefeldin A (Figure 2—figure supplement 1 compare columns 3–4 and 9–10).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data with brefeldin A treatment shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The lysosome protease inhibitor E-64 minimally affected APOE levels.
source: Additionally, the lysosome protease inhibitor E-64 minimally affected APOE levels; thus, making unlikely the contribution of lysosomes to the genotype-dependent differences in APOE levels (Figure 2—figure supplement 1 compare columns 5–6 and 11–12).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data with E-64 treatment shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: SLC25A1Δ/Δ SH-SY5Y cells increased secretion of APOE by approximately fourfold in both cells and conditioned media compared with wild-type cells.
source: Much like HAP1 cells, SLC25A1Δ/Δ cells increased secretion of APOE by ~fourfold, in both cells and conditioned media, compared with wild-type cells (Figure 2C, compare lanes 1 and 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by MesoScale ELISA data in SH-SY5Y cells shown in Figure 2C.

claim: APOE mRNA increased approximately threefold in SLC25A1Δ, SLC25A4Δ, and SLC25A1Δ/Δ mutant cells.
source: APOE mRNA increased ~threefold in all three mutant cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2D-F.

claim: The expression of cholesterol synthesis pathway genes was increased in SLC25A1Δ but not in SLC25A4Δ and SLC25A1Δ/Δ cells.
source: In contrast, the expression of cholesterol synthesis pathway genes was increased in SLC25A1Δ (Figure 2D) but not in SLC25A4Δ and SLC25A1Δ/Δ cells (Figure 2E and F).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2D-F.

claim: The upregulation of cholesterol synthesis pathway genes resulted in a significant increase of cholesterol and all cholesterol-ester species content in SLC25A1Δ cells.
source: The upregulation of cholesterol synthesis pathway genes resulted in a significant increase of cholesterol and all cholesterol-ester species content in SLC25A1Δ cells, as determined by mass spectrometry (Figure 2G and J).
evidence: The claim is supported by lipidomics data shown in Figure 2G and J.

claim: Triglyceride and other measured lipid families were similar in wild-type and SLC25A1Δ cells.
source: Triglyceride and other measured lipid families were similar in wild-type and SLC25A1Δ cells (Figure 2G and J).
evidence: The claim is supported by lipidomics data shown in Figure 2G and J.

claim: Cholesterol and cholesterol-ester species were not modified in SLC25A4Δ and SLC25A1Δ/Δ cells.
source: In contrast, cholesterol and cholesterol-ester species were not modified in SLC25A4Δ (Figure 2H and J) and SLC25A1Δ/Δ cells (Figure 2I and K), even though the expression of APOE was upregulated to the same extent in all these mutant cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by lipidomics data shown in Figure 2H-K.

claim: Increased APOE expression is unlikely to be coupled to an upregulation of cholesterol synthesis pathways.
source: These results make unlikely the hypothesis that increased APOE expression is coupled to an upregulation of cholesterol synthesis pathways.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that APOE is upregulated in all mutants but cholesterol synthesis is only upregulated in SLC25A1Δ.

claim: Complex I subunits were most affected in SLC25A1Δ cells.
source: We found that even though complex III was affected in both SLC25A1Δ and SLC25A4Δ cells (Figures 1K and 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A), the most pronounced defect was in the expression of complex I subunits in SLC25A1Δ cells (Figure 3A).
evidence: The claim is supported by proteomic analysis of electron transport chain subunits shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The most degraded subunits in SLC25A1Δ cells were those from complexes I and III.
source: These experiments revealed that the most degraded subunits were those from complexes I and III (Figure 3B).
evidence: The claim is supported by immunoblot analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: High molecular weight complexes containing NDUFS3, UQCRC2, and COX4 showed decreased expression in SLC25A1Δ cells by blue native electrophoresis.
source: We then analyzed respiratory complexes by blue native electrophoresis and found decreased expression of high molecular weight complexes containing NDUFS3, UQCRC2, and COX4, which correspond to subunits of the respiratory complexes I, III, and IV, respectively (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by blue native electrophoresis data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Two-dimensional gel electrophoresis showed that high molecular weight respiratory complexes containing subunits of complexes I and III were diminished in SLC25A1Δ cells.
source: Two-dimensional gel electrophoresis showed that high molecular weight respiratory complexes containing subunits of complexes I and III were diminished in SLC25A1Δ cells (Figure 3D).
evidence: The claim is supported by two-dimensional gel electrophoresis data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: SLC25A4Δ HAP1 cells had reduced levels of complex III subunits.
source: Similarly, SLC25A4Δ HAP1 cells had reduced levels of complex III subunits (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: The claim is supported by proteomic data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The SLC25A4 mutation affected the migration of complex III-containing supercomplexes in blue native electrophoresis.
source: thus affecting the migration of complex III-containing supercomplexes in blue native electrophoresis (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by blue native electrophoresis data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The effect of the SLC25A4 mutation on APOE expression was not due to a defect in the SLC25A4 transport activity.
source: The effect of the SLC25A4 mutation on APOE expression was not due to a defect in the SLC25A4 transport activity, as the SLC25A4 inhibitor bongkrekic acid did not increase the levels of APOE (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C, compare columns 1 with 2 and 3), even at concentrations that inhibit mitochondrial respiration to the same extent as the SLC25A4 mutation (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D; Gutiérrez-Aguilar and Baines, 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data with bongkrekic acid shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C-D and cited reference.

claim: NDUFS3 and NDUFAF7 CRISPR mutants compromised mitochondrial respiration.
source: NDUFS3 and NDUFAF7 CRISPR mutants compromised mitochondrial respiration, as shown by Seahorse oximetry (Figure 3E and H).
evidence: The claim is supported by Seahorse stress test data shown in Figure 3E and H.

claim: NDUFS3 and NDUFAF7 mutants increased the expression of APOE mRNA compared to reference housekeeping transcripts.
source: Both mutants increased the expression of APOE mRNA, as compared to reference housekeeping transcripts, (Figure 3F I, RER1 and VAMP2)
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3F and I.

claim: NDUFS3 and NDUFAF7 mutants increased APOE protein in cells and in conditioned media.
source: as well as APOE protein in cells and in conditioned media (Figure 3G and J).
evidence: The claim is supported by MesoScale ELISA data shown in Figure 3G and J.

claim: The integrity and function of complex I regulate APOE expression and secretion.
source: These results demonstrate that the integrity and function of complex I regulate APOE expression and secretion.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental results with NDUFS3 and NDUFAF7 mutants.

claim: SLC25A1Δ cells were more sensitive to low doses of antimycin than wild-type cells.
source: SLC25A1Δ cells were more sensitive to low doses of antimycin (Figure 3K), a phenotype predicted for cells with reduced content of complex III.
evidence: The claim is supported by Seahorse respiration data with antimycin treatment shown in Figure 3K.

claim: Antimycin addition increased APOE mRNA 3-fold in wild-type cells compared to vehicle.
source: Antimycin addition increased APOE mRNA 3-fold in wild-type cells as compared to vehicle (Figure 3L compare columns 9–10)
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3L.

claim: The expression of two housekeeping mRNAs, RER1 and PCBP1, was minimally affected by complex III inhibition with antimycin.
source: whereas the expression of two housekeeping mRNAs, RER1 and PCBP1, was minimally affected by complex III inhibition (Figure 3L compare columns 1–2 and 5–6).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3L.

claim: SLC25A1Δ cells doubled their APOE mRNA when treated with antimycin compared to vehicle-treated SLC25A1Δ cells.
source: SLC25A1Δ cells doubled their APOE mRNA when treated with antimycin as compared to vehicle-treated SLC25A1Δ cells (Figure 3L compare columns 11–12).
evidence: The claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3L.

claim: Antimycin increased APOE secretion in both wild-type and SLC25A1Δ cells by approximately 2-3 fold.
source: Antimycin also increased APOE secretion in both wild-type and SLC25A1Δ cells by ~2–3 fold (Figure 3M).
evidence: The claim is supported by MesoScale ELISA data shown in Figure 3M.

claim: No increase in APOE was detectable in cell lysates in both wild-type and SLC25A1Δ genotypes after antimycin treatment.
source: No such increase was detectable in cell lysates in both genotypes (Figure 3M).
evidence: The claim is supported by MesoScale ELISA data shown in Figure 3M.

claim: The effect of antimycin on APOE mRNA expression and protein secretion was additive with the SLC25A1Δ upregulation phenotype.
source: These data show that the effect of antimycin on APOE mRNA expression and protein secretion was additive with the SLC25A1Δ upregulation phenotype.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that antimycin further increases APOE in SLC25A1Δ cells.

claim: The expression of APOE is sensitive to complex III inhibition.
source: these results demonstrate that the expression of APOE is sensitive to complex III inhibition.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the antimycin treatment experiments.

claim: TMT proteomic analysis of SLC25A4Δ/Δ HEK293 cells revealed minimal changes in protein levels.
source: TMT proteomic analysis of whole cell extracts from SLC25A4Δ/Δ HEK293 cells revealed minimal changes in protein levels (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by TMT proteomic data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: 223 differentially expressed proteins were found in SLC25A4,5,6Δ/Δ triple knock-out cells.
source: In contrast, we found 223 differentially expressed proteins in SLC25A4,5,6Δ/Δ triple knock-out cells (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by TMT proteomic data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Of the 223 differentially expressed proteins in SLC25A4,5,6Δ/Δ triple knock-out cells, 32 were annotated to the secretome, including APOE.
source: Of these 223 proteins, 32 were annotated to the secretome, including APOE (Figure 4B and C).
evidence: The claim is supported by annotation analysis shown in Figure 4B and C.

claim: SLC25A4,5,6Δ/Δ triple knock-out cells increased APOE approximately twofold in both cell extracts and conditioned media compared with wild-type and SLC25A4Δ/Δ HEK293 cells.
source: We confirmed increased APOE levels by MesoScale ELISA in SLC25A4,5,6Δ/Δ triple knock-out cells, which increased APOE ~twofold, in both cell extracts and conditioned media, as compared with wild-type and SLC25A4Δ/Δ HEK293 cells (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by MesoScale ELISA data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Among the 223 differentially expressed proteins in SLC25A4,5,6Δ/Δ triple knock-out cells, 42 proteins were annotated to Mitocarta 3.0.
source: Among the 223 differentially expressed proteins, we also identified 42 proteins annotated to Mitocarta 3.0 (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by annotation analysis shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The 42 Mitocarta-annotated proteins in SLC25A4,5,6Δ/Δ triple knock-out cells included increased levels of 4 of the 10 subunits in complex III.
source: These included increased levels of 4 of the 10 subunits in complex III (Figure 4B and E).
evidence: The claim is supported by proteomic data shown in Figure 4B and E.

claim: Formation of complex III supercomplexes was selectively compromised in SLC25A4,5,6Δ/Δ triple knock-out cells.
source: Formation of complex III supercomplexes was selectively compromised in SLC25A4,5,6Δ/Δ triple knock-out cells as determined by blue native electrophoresis (Figure 4F).
evidence: The claim is supported by blue native electrophoresis data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Mitochondrial proteome modifications and defective supercomplexes formation reduced mitochondrial respiration by fivefold in SLC25A4,5,6Δ/Δ triple knock-out cells.
source: These mitochondrial proteome modifications and defective supercomplexes formation reduced mitochondrial respiration by fivefold in triple knock-out cells (Figure 4G).
evidence: The claim is supported by Seahorse stress test data shown in Figure 4G.

claim: Increased APOE expression is robustly observed in diverse cell types where the integrity of complex III of the electron transport chain is compromised.
source: We conclude that increased APOE expression is robustly observed in diverse cell types where the integrity of complex III of the electron transport chain is compromised.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental results in HEK293 cells with SLC25A4,5,6 triple knockout.

claim: Mutagenesis of COX7A2L did not affect APOE expression.
source: Mutagenesis of COX7A2L did not affect APOE expression but mutagenesis of HIGD1A increased APOE levels ~12-fold, both in cell lysates and conditioned media (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by MesoScale ELISA data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Mutagenesis of HIGD1A increased APOE levels approximately 12-fold in both cell lysates and conditioned media.
source: Mutagenesis of COX7A2L did not affect APOE expression but mutagenesis of HIGD1A increased APOE levels ~12-fold, both in cell lysates and conditioned media (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by MesoScale ELISA data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: COX18 and COX20 gene defects increased APOE expression to the same extent as HIGD1A.
source: We confirmed these findings with mutants in the complex IV assembly factors COX18 and 20 (Bourens and Barrientos, 2017; Nývltová et al., 2022). COX18 and 20 gene defects increased APOE expression to the same extent as HIGD1A (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by MesoScale ELISA data shown in Figure 5B and cited references.

claim: Mutagenesis of COX19 in HEK293 cells increased the expression of APOE protein in both cells and conditioned media by approximately 40-fold.
source: Mutagenesis of COX19 in HEK293 cells increased the expression of APOE protein in both cells and conditioned media by ~40-fold (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by MesoScale ELISA data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Mutagenesis of the metallochaperone COX17 in two SH-SY5Y mutants increased APOE levels.
source: We confirmed this finding in two SH-SY5Y mutants of the metallochaperone COX17 (Figure 5C, COX17Δ/Δ).
evidence: The claim is supported by MesoScale ELISA data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Mutagenesis of the SLC31A1 transporter increased APOE expression and secretion in two independent mutant isolates.
source: We decreased cytoplasmic copper availability by either eliminating copper uptake via mutagenesis of the SLC31A1 transporter (Figure 5D, SLC31A1Δ/Δ and Figure 5—figure supplement 1) or by expressing in ATP7A-null SH-SY5Y cells (ATP7AΔ/Δ and Figure 5—figure supplement 1) an ATP7A mutant that constitutively extrudes copper from cells due to mutagenesis of its endocytosis sorting signal (Figure 5E and Figure 5—figure supplement 1, ATP7A-LL) (Petris et al., 1998; Zhu et al., 2016). Both forms of cytoplasmic copper reduction increased APOE expression and secretion in two independent mutant or clonal isolates (Figure 5D–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by MesoScale ELISA data shown in Figure 5D and cited references.

claim: Expression of an ATP7A mutant that constitutively extrudes copper from cells increased APOE expression and secretion in two independent clonal isolates.
source: or by expressing in ATP7A-null SH-SY5Y cells (ATP7AΔ/Δ and Figure 5—figure supplement 1) an ATP7A mutant that constitutively extrudes copper from cells due to mutagenesis of its endocytosis sorting signal (Figure 5E and Figure 5—figure supplement 1, ATP7A-LL) (Petris et al., 1998; Zhu et al., 2016). Both forms of cytoplasmic copper reduction increased APOE expression and secretion in two independent mutant or clonal isolates (Figure 5D–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by MesoScale ELISA data shown in Figure 5E and cited references.

claim: Elimination of ATP7A alone did not increase APOE expression.
source: Elimination of ATP7A alone did not increase APOE expression (Figure 5F, ATP7AΔ/Δ).
evidence: The claim is supported by MesoScale ELISA data shown in Figure 5F.

claim: Mutagenesis of SLC25A3 increased the expression and secretion of APOE protein in HAP1 cells.
source: Mutagenesis of SLC25A3, also increased the expression and secretion of APOE protein in HAP1 cells (Figure 5G).
evidence: The claim is supported by MesoScale ELISA data shown in Figure 5G.

claim: Pharmacological and genetic approaches to reduction of cytoplasmic copper robustly increased APOE mRNA compared to wild-type cells.
source: These pharmacological and genetic approaches to reduction of cytoplasmic copper robustly increased APOE mRNA as compared to wild-type cells (Figure 5H), while levels of a housekeeping gene, TBP, were unchanged.
evidence: The claim is supported by NanoString mRNA quantification data shown in Figure 5H.

claim: Levels of the housekeeping gene TBP were unchanged by reduction of cytoplasmic copper.
source: These pharmacological and genetic approaches to reduction of cytoplasmic copper robustly increased APOE mRNA as compared to wild-type cells (Figure 5H), while levels of a housekeeping gene, TBP, were unchanged.
evidence: The claim is supported by NanoString mRNA quantification data shown in Figure 5H.

claim: Impairing complex IV biogenesis, directly or indirectly, increases the expression of APOE transcript and protein in diverse cell lines.
source: These results demonstrate that impairing complex IV biogenesis, directly or indirectly, increases the expression of APOE transcript and protein in diverse cell lines.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental results with various complex IV-related mutants.

claim: Diverse mechanisms converging on respiratory chain function and assembly can induce the expression and secretion of APOE.
source: Along with our experiments targeting complexes I and III, these findings support the concept that diverse mechanisms converging on respiratory chain function and assembly can induce the expression and secretion of APOE.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental results targeting different respiratory chain complexes.

claim: APOE negatively and significantly correlated with basal oxygen consumption (r=-0.62, p=0.022).
source: APOE negatively and significantly correlated with basal oxygen consumption (–0.62, Figure 5J, r=−0.62, p=0.022).
evidence: The claim is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 5J.

claim: The correlation of APOE expression with the rate of extracellular acidification did not differ from zero (p=0.2).
source: The correlation of APOE expression with the rate of extracellular acidification did not differ from zero (Figure 5J, p=0.2 and Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The claim is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 5J and Figure 5—figure supplement 3.

claim: Mutants of the carnitine transporter SLC25A20 increased APOE levels despite normal respiration.
source: However, we identified an exception in mutants of the carnitine transporter SLC25A20 that increased APOE levels despite normal respiration (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: Respiratory chain integrity and activity rather than glycolytic adaptations in mutants affecting the electron transport chain modulate APOE expression.
source: These findings support the idea that respiratory chain integrity and activity rather than glycolytic adaptations in mutants affecting the electron transport chain modulate APOE expression.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the correlation analyses of APOE with oxygen consumption and extracellular acidification.

claim: Treatment with the antioxidant N-acetyl cysteine did not affect APOE mRNA levels in wild-type or SLC25A1Δ cells.
source: We ruled out accumulation of reactive oxygen species as a causal mechanism for increased APOE, as treatment with the antioxidant N-acetyl cysteine did not affect APOE mRNA levels in wild-type or SLC25A1Δ cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 5).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 5.

claim: Activation of the mitochondrial stress response with doxycycline modestly increased the secretion of APOE in SLC25A1Δ cells but not in wild-type cells.
source: We found that activation of the mitochondrial stress response with doxycycline (Quirós et al., 2017) modestly increased the secretion of APOE in SLC25A1Δ cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 5 panel D columns 7–8) but not in wild-type cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 5 panel D columns 5–6)
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 5 and cited reference.

claim: Wild-type cells robustly activated the mitochondrial stress response after doxycycline incubation.
source: even though wild-type cells robustly activated the mitochondrial stress response after doxycycline incubation (Figure 5—figure supplement 5 panel E).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 5.

claim: FCCP failed to induce APOE expression in HAP1 cells.
source: Furthermore, FCCP, also a potent activator of the mitochondrial stress response (Quirós et al., 2017) failed to induce APOE expression in HAP1 cells, even though inhibition of either complexes I or V with piericidin A or oligomycin increased APOE levels (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2 and cited reference.

claim: The ATF4-dependent stress response alone cannot account for elevated APOE expression and secretion.
source: Thus, the ATF4-dependent stress response alone cannot account for elevated APOE expression and secretion.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the doxycycline and FCCP experiments.

claim: Astrocytes increased APOE protein expression twofold after antimycin treatment.
source: Astrocytes increased APOE protein expression twofold after antimycin treatment (Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is supported by MesoScale ELISA data in iPSC-derived astrocytes shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Astrocytic APOE increases after antimycin treatment were detected both in cell lysates and conditioned media.
source: These astrocytic APOE increases were detected both in cell lysates and conditioned media (Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is supported by MesoScale ELISA data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Neuronal cells failed to increase APOE expression after exposure to antimycin.
source: In contrast, neuronal cells failed to increase APOE expression after exposure to antimycin (Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is supported by MesoScale ELISA data in iPSC-derived neurons shown in Figure 6A.

claim: APOE was not detected in neuronal conditioned media.
source: We did not detect APOE in neuronal conditioned media (not shown).
evidence: The claim is stated based on experimental observations not shown in figures.

claim: APOE expression and secretion are modulated by intoxication of the electron transport chain in iPSC-derived human astrocytes but not neurons.
source: These findings show that APOE expression and secretion are modulated by intoxication of the electron transport chain in iPSC-derived human astrocytes but not neurons.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the antimycin treatment experiments in neurons and astrocytes.

claim: APOE mRNA was upregulated sixfold in mutant HAP1 cells and 1.5 times in antimycin-treated astrocytes compared to a housekeeping control, TBP.
source: Among these genes, APOE mRNA was upregulated sixfold in mutant HAP1 cells and 1.5 times in antimycin-treated astrocytes as compared to a housekeeping control, TBP (Figure 6C).
evidence: The claim is supported by NanoString mRNA quantification data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The genes upregulated in antimycin-treated astrocytes were significantly enriched in genes annotated to the secretome compared to the content of secretome-annotated genes built into the panel.
source: The genes upregulated in antimycin-treated astrocytes were significantly enriched in genes annotated to the secretome, as compared to the content of secretome-annotated genes built into the panel (Figure 6D, compare enrichment factors of 2.8 and 1.6, respectively).
evidence: The claim is supported by enrichment analysis shown in Figure 6D.

claim: The enrichment of altered secretory transcripts induced by mitochondrial damage was similar to changes in mitochondrially annotated transcripts in SLC25A1Δ and SLC25A4Δ HAP1 cells and antimycin-treated astrocytes.
source: Like in SLC25A1Δ and SLC25A4Δ HAP1 cells, this enrichment of altered secretory transcripts induced by mitochondrial damage was similar to changes in mitochondrially annotated transcripts.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the enrichment analysis comparing secretome and mitochondrial annotations.

claim: Four upregulated mRNAs were common to SLC25A1Δ, SLC25A4Δ HAP1 cells, and iPSC-derived astrocytes treated with antimycin: APOE, TSPAN18, PTPN6, and LOX.
source: We identified four upregulated mRNAs common to these three experimental conditions (Figure 6E, APOE, TSPAN18, PTPN6, and LOX).
evidence: The claim is supported by Circos plot analysis shown in Figure 6E.

claim: The number of shared upregulated hits increased to 45 mRNAs when considering shared functional annotations.
source: The number of hits increased to 45 upregulated mRNAs when considering shared functional annotations (Figure 6E).
evidence: The claim is supported by Circos plot analysis shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Functional annotations of shared upregulated mRNAs were mostly related to cytokine signaling ontologies.
source: These functional annotations were mostly related to cytokine signaling ontologies (Figure 6F and R -HSA-1280215 and GO:0034097 Log q-value=−25.19 and –18.18).
evidence: The claim is supported by Metascape ontology analysis shown in Figure 6F.

claim: There was no correlation in gene expression between the 85 upregulated genes in antimycin-treated astrocytes and the changes in expression of these mRNAs in astrocytes after inflammatory LPS administration to elicit the A1 transcriptional phenotype.
source: To explore whether the 85 upregulated genes in antimycin-treated astrocytes were part of a neurotoxic A1 reactive astrocyte phenotype associated with neurodegeneration, we compared the fold of induction of these transcripts with the changes in expression of these mRNAs in astrocytes after inflammatory LPS administration to elicit the A1 transcriptional phenotype (Liddelow et al., 2017). There was no correlation in gene expression among these datasets (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1 and cited reference.

claim: Increased expression of APOE induced by disruption of mitochondria co-occurs with inflammatory mechanisms, which are distinct from known expression signatures of reactive astrocytes induced by LPS.
source: These results suggest that increased expression of APOE induced by disruption of mitochondria co-occurs with inflammatory mechanisms, which are distinct from known expression signatures of reactive astrocytes induced by LPS.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the lack of correlation with A1 reactive astrocyte phenotype and the presence of cytokine signaling ontologies.

claim: APOE expression across all ages inversely correlated with the expression of complex I, II, and IV subunits in 5xFAD but not in wild-type animals.
source: APOE expression across all ages inversely correlated with the expression of complex I, II, and IV subunits in 5xFAD but not in wild-type animals (Figure 7B–C).
evidence: The claim is supported by correlation analysis in 5xFAD mouse cortex shown in Figure 7B-C.

claim: The expression of respiratory complex subunits varied with age in wild-type animals.
source: The expression of respiratory complex subunits varied with age in wild-type animals (Figure 7D, gray symbols).
evidence: The claim is supported by proteomic data across ages shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Complex I subunits increased to a plateau at 6 months of age in wild-type cortex.
source: For example, complex I subunits increased to a plateau at 6 months of age in wild-type cortex (Figure 7D, gray symbols).
evidence: The claim is supported by proteomic data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: APOE expression remained constant with age in wild-type animals.
source: APOE expression remained constant with age in wild-type animals (Figure 7D, gray symbols).
evidence: The claim is supported by proteomic data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: APOE expression progressively increased sevenfold in 5xFAD animals.
source: However, APOE expression progressively increased sevenfold in 5xFAD animals (Figure 7D, blue symbols)
evidence: The claim is supported by proteomic data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Most electron transport chain complexes decreased their expression with age in 5xFAD animals.
source: while most electron transport chain complexes decreased their expression with age in 5xFAD animals (Figure 7C–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by proteomic data shown in Figure 7C-D.

claim: A significant decrease in the expression of complex I and COX7C was detected in 5xFAD cortex.
source: We detected a significant decrease in the expression of complex I and one of three mitochondrial Alzheimer's disease risk factors, COX7C, in 5xFAD cortex (Bellenguez et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by proteomic data and cited reference about COX7C as an Alzheimer's risk factor.

claim: Changes in respiratory chain protein levels preceded the APOE increase observed at 6 months of age in 5xFAD mutant animals.
source: Importantly, these changes in respiratory chain protein levels preceded the APOE increase observed at 6 months of age in mutant animals (Figure 7D).
evidence: The claim is supported by temporal analysis of proteomic data shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Changes in the expression of complex I and COX7C are followed by later increases in APOE in diseased cortex.
source: These results reveal that changes in the expression of complex I and COX7C are followed by later increases in APOE in diseased cortex.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the temporal analysis showing respiratory chain changes precede APOE increases.

claim: Brain protein expression representing the SLC25A1Δ upregulated mRNAs correlated with an accelerated cognitive decline (r=-0.607, p<1.03e-11) in the Banner cohort.
source: In the Banner cohort, the brain protein expression representing the SLC25A1Δ upregulated mRNAs correlated with an accelerated cognitive decline (r=−0.607, p<1.03e-11, Figure 7E).
evidence: The claim is supported by correlation analysis with cognitive trajectory shown in Figure 7E.

claim: Brain protein expression representing the downregulated mRNAs associated with a slower rate of cognitive decline in the Banner cohort proteomes (r=0.472, p<4.45e-07).
source: In contrast, the brain protein expression representing the downregulated mRNAs associated with a slower rate of cognitive decline in the Banner cohort proteomes (r=0.472, p<4.45e-07, Figure 7E).
evidence: The claim is supported by correlation analysis with cognitive trajectory shown in Figure 7E.

claim: Increased brain expression of the differentially expressed proteins in the SLC25A1Δ TMT proteome correlated with accelerated cognitive decline (r=-0.537, p<4.45e-07) in the Banner cohort.
source: Like the SLC25A1Δ upregulated mRNAs, increased brain expression of the differentially expressed proteins in the SLC25A1Δ TMT proteome (Figure 1B) also correlated with accelerated cognitive decline (r=−0.537, p<4.45e-07, Fig. Figure 7E).
evidence: The claim is supported by correlation analysis with cognitive trajectory shown in Figure 7E.

claim: The SLC25A1Δ upregulated mRNAs and proteome shared APOE and sterol synthesis as a top ontology.
source: The SLC25A1Δ upregulated mRNAs and proteome shared APOE and sterol synthesis as a top ontology (Figure 1O–P).
evidence: The claim is supported by gene ontology analysis shown in Figure 1O-P.

claim: Genes and proteins sensitive to SLC25A1 expression regulate cellular processes important for cognition.
source: These data suggest that genes and proteins sensitive to SLC25A1 expression regulate cellular processes important for cognition.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the correlations between SLC25A1-sensitive gene expression and cognitive trajectory.

claim: Greater expression of proteins belonging to the SLC25A1 interactome strongly correlated with a rapid cognitive decline in the Banner cohort (r=-0.527, p<9.92e-08).
source: In line with this reasoning, we found that greater expression of proteins belonging to the SLC25A1 interactome strongly correlated with a rapid cognitive decline in the Banner cohort (r=−0.527, p<9.92e-08, Figure 7E).
evidence: The claim is supported by correlation analysis with cognitive trajectory shown in Figure 7E.

claim: The mitochondrial ribosome correlated poorly with cognitive decline in the Banner cohort compared to the SLC25A1 datasets.
source: The mitochondrial ribosome correlated poorly with cognitive decline in the Banner cohort as compared to the SLC25A1 datasets even though the SLC25A1 interactome dataset was of a similar size to the mitochondrial ribosome dataset (Figure 7E, compare SLC25A1 interactome composed of 75 proteins and mitochondrial ribosome composed of 77 proteins).
evidence: The claim is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 7E.

claim: The expression of cytoplasmic ribosomal proteins did not correlate with the cognitive trajectory of the Banner subjects (r=-0.24 and p=0.249).
source: In addition, the expression of cytoplasmic ribosomal proteins did not correlate with the cognitive trajectory of the Banner subjects (r=−0.24 and p=0.249, Figure 7E).
evidence: The claim is supported by correlation analysis shown in Figure 7E.

claim: A network of mitochondrial proteins, including the respiratory chain and several members of the SLC25A transporter family, regulates APOE expression and other cellular processes modulating cognition during aging.
source: Taken together, our data suggest that a network of mitochondrial proteins, including the respiratory chain and several members of the SLC25A transporter family, regulates APOE expression and other cellular processes modulating cognition during aging.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the correlation analyses of SLC25A1-related datasets with cognitive trajectory.

claim: Mutations in nuclear-encoded mitochondrial transporter genes, SLC25A1 and SLC25A4, modify the secretome and mitochondrially annotated proteome to a similar extent.
source: Here, we report our discovery that mutations in nuclear-encoded mitochondrial transporter genes, SLC25A1 and SLC25A4, modify the secretome and mitochondrially annotated proteome to a similar extent.
evidence: The claim is supported by proteomic analysis showing similar enrichment of secretome and mitochondrial proteins.

claim: Mutations in either SLC25A1 or SLC25A4 upregulated the expression and secretion of the lipoprotein APOE in diverse cellular systems.
source: Intriguingly, mutations in either one of these mitochondrial transporters upregulated the expression and secretion of the lipoprotein APOE in diverse cellular systems.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data across multiple cell types.

claim: This mitochondrial-dependent APOE upregulation phenotype occurs in response to loss of integrity of the electron transport chain secondary to either SLC25A1 or SLC25A4 mutagenesis.
source: We show that this mitochondrial-dependent APOE upregulation phenotype occurs in response to loss of integrity of the electron transport chain secondary to either SLC25A1 or SLC25A4 mutagenesis.
evidence: The claim is supported by blue native electrophoresis and proteomic data showing electron transport chain defects.

claim: Disruption of the assembly and function of electron transport chain complexes I, III, and IV increases APOE.
source: We demonstrate that disruption of the assembly and function of electron transport chain complexes I, III, and IV also increases APOE
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data with mutants targeting different respiratory complexes.

claim: A main initiating event in a cascade that increases APOE levels is the disruption of electron transport chain integrity and function.
source: arguing that a main initiating event in a cascade that increases APOE levels is the disruption of electron transport chain integrity and function.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the experimental results showing various ways of disrupting the electron transport chain all lead to increased APOE.

claim: Both mutations that directly or indirectly compromise the electron transport chain increase APOE levels.
source: Both mutations that directly or indirectly compromise the electron transport chain increase APOE levels.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data with various mutants affecting the electron transport chain.

claim: Genetic disruption of copper loading into complex IV with mutants directly targeting copper loading factors, such as COX17 and COX19, increased APOE levels.
source: For example, genetic disruption of copper loading into complex IV with mutants directly targeting copper loading factors, such as COX17 and COX19, increased APOE levels.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data with COX17 and COX19 mutants.

claim: Indirectly disrupting cellular copper homeostasis at the plasma membrane (SLC31A1 and ATP7A), the mitochondrial inner membrane (SLC25A3), or by pharmacological copper chelation with BCS all affect complex IV and increase APOE levels.
source: A similar APOE phenotype is obtained by indirectly disrupting cellular copper homeostasis at the plasma membrane (SLC31A1 and ATP7A), the mitochondrial inner membrane (SLC25A3), or by pharmacological copper chelation with BCS, all conditions that affect complex IV (Boulet et al., 2018; Cobine et al., 2021; Guthrie et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data with various copper-related mutants and treatments, and cited references.

claim: The mitochondrial protein network modulating APOE expression includes proteins encoded by prioritized genes within Alzheimer's disease risk loci necessary for electron transport chain complex I assembly and function.
source: The mitochondrial protein network modulating APOE expression includes proteins encoded by prioritized genes within Alzheimer's disease risk loci necessary for electron transport chain complex I assembly and function (de Rojas et al., 2021; Kunkle et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data with NDUFS3 and NDUFAF7 mutants and cited references about Alzheimer's risk loci.

claim: This mitochondrial regulation of APOE expression extends to brain cells, iPSC-derived human astrocytes, and co-occurs with an inflammatory gene expression response.
source: Furthermore, we show that this mitochondrial regulation of APOE expression extends to brain cells, iPSC-derived human astrocytes, and co-occurs with an inflammatory gene expression response.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data in iPSC-derived astrocytes and NanoString analysis.

claim: Mitochondria robustly regulate APOE expression and secretion, placing them in a novel position upstream of APOE.
source: Together, our data demonstrate that mitochondria robustly regulate APOE expression and secretion, placing them in a novel position upstream of APOE.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the comprehensive experimental data showing mitochondrial dysfunction leads to increased APOE.

claim: This mitochondria-to-APOE mechanism may operate in the pathogenesis of dementia.
source: We propose that this mitochondria-to-APOE mechanism may operate in the pathogenesis of dementia, a proposition supported by our protein expression correlation studies in mouse Alzheimer's brains and aging human brains.
evidence: The claim is speculative but supported by correlation studies in 5xFAD mice and human brain cohorts.

claim: There are other intramitochondrial mechanisms connecting mitochondria to APOE expression and secretion beyond the loss of integrity of the electron transport chain.
source: Our results support the idea that there are other intramitochondrial mechanisms connecting mitochondria to APOE expression and secretion beyond the loss of integrity of the electron transport chain.
evidence: The claim is inferred from observations with SLC25A20 and ACLY mutants that increase APOE despite normal respiration or different mechanisms.

claim: Mutagenesis of the mitochondrial carnitine transporter SLC25A20 upregulated APOE despite these cells respiring normally and having wild-type levels of respiratory chain subunits.
source: Mutagenesis of the mitochondrial carnitine transporter SLC25A20 also upregulated APOE, despite these cells respiring normally and having wild-type levels of respiratory chain subunits.
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: Mutagenesis of ACLY, a cytosolic enzyme that controls the synthesis of acetyl-CoA using citrate as a substrate, increases APOE expression.
source: Similarly, mutagenesis of a cytosolic enzyme that controls the synthesis of acetyl-CoA using citrate as a substrate, ACLY, also increases APOE expression (Figure 5—figure supplement 4).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 4.

claim: In addition to the integrity of the electron transport chain, there are other mitochondrial and cytoplasmic mechanisms regulating APOE expression.
source: Thus, we postulate that in addition to the integrity of the electron transport chain, there are other mitochondrial and cytoplasmic mechanisms regulating APOE expression.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observations with SLC25A20 and ACLY mutants.

claim: Glycolytic adaptations in the mitochondrial mutants are unlikely to account for the APOE phenotype.
source: These observations make it unlikely that glycolytic adaptations in the mitochondrial mutants used in our studies could account for the APOE phenotype.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the lack of correlation between APOE and extracellular acidification rate.

claim: Decreased ATP levels are unlikely to mediate increased APOE protein levels.
source: If decreased ATP levels mediate increased APOE protein levels, SLC25A1-null cells should display activation of the AMPK pathway at baseline. We found that, while SLC25A1-null cells are sensitized to respond to an AMPK-activating drug, the pathway is minimally active in the cells at baseline (Figure 5—figure supplement 5).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the AMPK activation experiments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 5.

claim: ATP levels between SLC25A1-null and wild-type cells do not differ.
source: This aligns with our previous finding that ATP levels between SLC25A1-null and wild-type cells do not differ (Gokhale et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by a cited previous study.

claim: Increased APOE resulting from mitochondrial dysfunction is not dependent on cholesterol synthesis pathways.
source: Thus, increased APOE resulting from mitochondrial dysfunction is not dependent on cholesterol synthesis pathways.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that APOE is upregulated in mutants without upregulation of cholesterol synthesis.

claim: The ATF4-dependent stress response alone cannot account for elevated APOE expression and secretion.
source: Despite stress response activation, cellular and secreted levels of APOE protein were unaffected besides a mild increase in secretion in the SLC25A1-null cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 5). Furthermore, FCCP, also a potent activator of the mitochondrial stress response (Quirós et al., 2017) failed to induce APOE expression in HAP1 cells, even though inhibition of either complexes I or V with piericidin A or oligomycin increased APOE levels (Figure 3—figure supplement 2). Thus, the ATF4-dependent stress response alone cannot account for elevated APOE expression and secretion.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the doxycycline and FCCP experiments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 5 and Figure 3—figure supplement 2, and cited reference.

claim: Redox imbalance is unlikely to account for increased APOE expression.
source: A fourth mechanism that could account for the increased APOE expression is dependent on redox imbalance. We think this mechanism is unlikely because the antioxidant N-acetyl cysteine decreased the expression of the mitochondrial glutathione-disulfide reductase in both wild-type and SLC25A1-null cells, but it did not change APOE mRNA levels (Figure 5—figure supplement 5).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the N-acetyl cysteine treatment experiments shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 5.

claim: Neither common predicted transcription factors nor transcription factors known to regulate APOE transcription such as LXRs or C/EBPβ were found in the SLC25A1 and SLC25A4 upregulated transcriptomes.
source: Finally, we looked for transcriptional signatures in the SLC25A1 and SLC25A4 upregulated transcriptomes and found neither common predicted transcription factors that could account for the changes in gene expression in both genotypes, nor transcription factors known to regulate APOE transcription such as LXRs or C/EBPβ (Fig. S6C) (Laffitte et al., 2001; Xia et al., 2021).
evidence: The claim is supported by transcriptional analysis and cited references about APOE transcription factors.

claim: A screen targeting large swaths of the genome in astrocytes and mutant cell lines would be an effective method for uncovering further mechanisms by which mitochondria contribute to APOE expression regulation.
source: We suggest that a screen targeting large swaths of the genome in astrocytes and mutant cell lines used in this study would be an effective method for uncovering further mechanisms by which mitochondria contribute to APOE expression regulation.
evidence: The claim is a speculative suggestion for future research.

claim: Mitochondrial distress regulates the secretion of inflammatory cytokines and type I interferons.
source: Our findings expand previous work demonstrating that mitochondrial distress regulates the secretion of inflammatory cytokines and type I interferons (Dhir et al., 2018; Riley and Tait, 2020; Shimada et al., 2012; West et al., 2015)
evidence: The claim is supported by cited references about mitochondrial regulation of cytokines and interferons.

claim: Mitochondrial distress regulates the secretion of the growth factor mitokines GDF15 and FGF21.
source: the growth factor mitokines GDF15 and FGF21 (Chung et al., 2017; Kim et al., 2013)
evidence: The claim is supported by cited references about mitokines.

claim: Mitochondrial distress regulates the production of mitochondrially-derived peptides encoded in the mitochondrial genome.
source: the production of mitochondrially-derived peptides encoded in the mitochondrial genome (Kim et al., 2017)
evidence: The claim is supported by cited reference about mitochondrially-derived peptides.

claim: Mitochondrial distress regulates the secretion of alpha fetoprotein in hepatocytes.
source: and alpha fetoprotein in hepatocytes (Jett et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by cited reference about alpha fetoprotein.

claim: APOE is the first apolipoprotein whose expression and secretion is modulated by mutations affecting mitochondria.
source: First, we identified the first apolipoprotein whose expression and secretion is modulated by mutations affecting mitochondria.
evidence: The claim is based on the novelty of the findings in this study.

claim: APOE is a harbinger of an extended upregulation of the secreted proteome mediated by mitochondria.
source: Second, while we focus on APOE, we think this apolipoprotein is a harbinger of an extended upregulation of the secreted proteome mediated by mitochondria (Uhlén et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation of widespread secretome changes in the proteomic data and cited reference.

claim: The importance of secreted proteome changes can be inferred from its extent and magnitude, which is on par with the changes observed in the mitochondrially annotated proteome.
source: The importance of this secreted proteome change can be inferred from its extent and magnitude, which is on par with the changes we observed in the mitochondrially annotated proteome.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the enrichment analysis comparing secretome and mitochondrial proteome changes.

claim: Mitochondrial regulation of the secreted proteome is a more common process than previously appreciated.
source: Our findings add to the growing notion that mitochondrial regulation of the secreted proteome is a more common process than previously appreciated (Jett et al., 2022; Sturm et al., 2023).
evidence: The claim is supported by the findings in this study and cited references.

claim: All three experimental conditions (SLC25A1Δ cells, SLC25A4Δ cells, and antimycin-treated astrocytes) converged on common hits whose number increased when considering hits belonging to shared ontologies.
source: Although SLC25A4Δ cells had a paucity of significant hits compared with SLC25A1Δ cells and antimycin-treated astrocytes, we found that all three experimental conditions converged on common hits whose number increased when considering hits belonging to shared ontologies.
evidence: The claim is supported by NanoString analysis and ontology analysis.

claim: All cells (SLC25A1Δ, SLC25A4Δ, and antimycin-treated astrocytes) showed increased levels of secreted cytokines.
source: All cells showed increased levels of secreted cytokines and gene ontologies associated with their transcriptional profiles were enriched for cytokine signaling pathways.
evidence: The claim is supported by NanoString analysis and ontology analysis.

claim: Gene ontologies associated with the transcriptional profiles of SLC25A1Δ, SLC25A4Δ, and antimycin-treated astrocytes were enriched for cytokine signaling pathways.
source: All cells showed increased levels of secreted cytokines and gene ontologies associated with their transcriptional profiles were enriched for cytokine signaling pathways.
evidence: The claim is supported by ontology analysis.

claim: APOE upregulation in response to mitochondrial dysfunction could be part of an inflammatory response initiated by mitochondria.
source: Thus, our data suggest that APOE upregulation in response to mitochondrial dysfunction could be part of an inflammatory response initiated by mitochondria.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the NanoString and ontology analyses showing co-occurrence of APOE upregulation with inflammatory gene expression.

claim: Mitochondria drive inflammatory signaling in the nervous system.
source: Although mitochondria are often viewed as downstream targets of neuroinflammation, our results with antimycin-treated astrocytes add to growing evidence that mitochondria drive inflammatory signaling in the nervous system (Bader and Winklhofer, 2020; Joshi et al., 2019; Lin et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by the findings in antimycin-treated astrocytes and cited references.

claim: APOE particles play necessary roles in handling toxic lipids by shuttling them between cell types.
source: APOE particles play necessary roles in handling toxic lipids by shuttling them between cell types, with differential effects depending on the cell type from which the APOE particle originated, the lipid species loaded in the particle, and the fate of the lipid-loaded particle (Guttenplan et al., 2021; Ioannou et al., 2019; Liu et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by cited references about APOE function.

claim: Either APOE-dependent removal of toxic factors from SLC25A1 mutant cells, or wild-type conditioned media delivering a factor missing from SLC25A1 mutant media, could explain the finding that dialyzed conditioned media from SLC25A1 mutant cells cannot support their own growth.
source: We speculate that either APOE-dependent removal of toxic factors from SLC25A1 mutant cells, or wild-type conditioned media delivering a factor missing from SLC25A1 mutant media, could explain our finding that dialyzed conditioned media from SLC25A1 mutant cells cannot support their own growth.
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning based on the conditioned media experiments.

claim: Astrocytes play a prominent role in carrying and processing toxic lipids in the brain through APOE-dependent mechanisms.
source: Astrocytes play a prominent role in carrying and processing toxic lipids in the brain through APOE-dependent mechanisms.
evidence: The claim is based on established knowledge about astrocyte function.

claim: APOE released from astrocytes following antimycin administration may not sustain either astrocytes and/or neurons.
source: Since we observed increased APOE secretion in astrocytes, but not neurons, in response to antimycin, we speculate that APOE released from astrocytes following antimycin administration may not sustain either astrocytes and/or neurons.
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning based on the antimycin experiments in astrocytes and neurons.

claim: The APOE E4 allele is the strongest genetic risk factor for sporadic Alzheimer's disease.
source: The APOE E4 allele is the strongest genetic risk factor for sporadic Alzheimer's disease and APOE, along with amyloidogenic processing of the amyloid precursor protein (APP) into Aβ, is thought of as an initiating and driving factor in disease etiology (Frisoni et al., 2022; Huang and Mahley, 2014; Mahley, 2023; Martens et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by cited references about APOE4 and Alzheimer's disease.

claim: APOE, along with amyloidogenic processing of APP into Aβ, is thought of as an initiating and driving factor in Alzheimer's disease etiology.
source: The APOE E4 allele is the strongest genetic risk factor for sporadic Alzheimer's disease and APOE, along with amyloidogenic processing of the amyloid precursor protein (APP) into Aβ, is thought of as an initiating and driving factor in disease etiology (Frisoni et al., 2022; Huang and Mahley, 2014; Mahley, 2023; Martens et al., 2022).
evidence: The claim is supported by cited references about APOE and Alzheimer's disease.

claim: Mitochondrial dysfunction is acknowledged as an important factor in Alzheimer's disease.
source: While mitochondrial dysfunction is acknowledged as an important factor in Alzheimer's disease, mitochondria are typically placed downstream of Aβ and APOE, with Aβ or the APOE4 allele perturbing mitochondrial function (Area-Gomez et al., 2020; Chen et al., 2011; Mahley, 2023; Orr et al., 2019; Tambini et al., 2016; Yin et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by cited references about mitochondrial dysfunction in Alzheimer's disease.

claim: Mitochondria are typically placed downstream of Aβ and APOE, with Aβ or the APOE4 allele perturbing mitochondrial function.
source: While mitochondrial dysfunction is acknowledged as an important factor in Alzheimer's disease, mitochondria are typically placed downstream of Aβ and APOE, with Aβ or the APOE4 allele perturbing mitochondrial function (Area-Gomez et al., 2020; Chen et al., 2011; Mahley, 2023; Orr et al., 2019; Tambini et al., 2016; Yin et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by cited references about the relationship between APOE, Aβ, and mitochondria.

claim: Some have proposed that mitochondria act as upstream factors in Alzheimer's pathogenesis through metabolic and bioenergetic effects.
source: Some have proposed that mitochondria act as upstream factors in Alzheimer's pathogenesis through metabolic and bioenergetic effects (Rangaraju et al., 2018; Swerdlow, 2018; Wang et al., 2020).
evidence: The claim is supported by cited references about mitochondria as upstream factors in Alzheimer's disease.

claim: Mitochondria could participate in Alzheimer's pathogenesis through modulation of APOE allele-dependent mechanisms.
source: We argue that mitochondria could also participate in Alzheimer's pathogenesis through modulation of APOE allele-dependent mechanisms.
evidence: The claim is a novel proposition based on the findings of this study.

claim: The increased expression of APOE, which is inversely correlated with the expression of respiratory chain subunits in the 5xFAD mouse model, supports the proposition that mitochondria participate in Alzheimer's pathogenesis through modulation of APOE.
source: The increased expression of APOE, which is inversely correlated with the expression of respiratory chain subunits in the 5xFAD mouse model, supports this proposition (Figure 7).
evidence: The claim is supported by correlation analysis in the 5xFAD mouse model shown in Figure 7.

claim: Increased expression of APOE E4 downstream of mitochondrial dysfunction could either initiate or exacerbate the effects of the APOE4 allele in neurodegenerative processes, since APOE4 is prone to aggregation and poor lipidation.
source: For example, increased expression of APOE E4 downstream of mitochondrial dysfunction could either initiate or exacerbate the effects of the APOE4 allele in neurodegenerative processes, since APOE4 is prone to aggregation and poor lipidation (Gong et al., 2002; Hatters et al., 2006; Hubin et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is speculative reasoning based on the findings and cited references about APOE4 properties.

claim: The findings open the possibility that mitochondria could act as initiators or drivers of Alzheimer's pathogenesis through modulation of APOE-dependent disease processes.
source: Our findings open the possibility that mitochondria could act as initiators or drivers of Alzheimer's pathogenesis through modulation of APOE-dependent disease processes.
evidence: The claim is a speculative proposition based on the findings of this study.

claim: The correlation of expression levels in the prefrontal cortex of proteins dysregulated in the SLC25A1 proteome and transcriptome with human cognitive trajectory provides evidence for the conception that mitochondria act as initiators or drivers of Alzheimer's pathogenesis.
source: The correlation of expression levels in the prefrontal cortex of proteins dysregulated in the SLC25A1 proteome and transcriptome with human cognitive trajectory provides evidence for this conception.
evidence: The claim is supported by correlation analysis in the Banner cohort.

claim: Mitochondria influence brain function and cognition in part through modulation of the secretome, including a novel role in regulation of APOE expression and secretion.
source: Together, our work supports the idea that mitochondria influence brain function and cognition in part through modulation of the secretome, including a novel role in regulation of APOE expression and secretion.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the comprehensive findings of the study.
